leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Adverbs of Frequency
leadIn.content: How often do you drink coffee? Alex always drinks coffee in the morning, usually goes for a walk, and never smokes.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Adverbs of Frequency?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Adverbs of Frequency require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Adverbs of Frequency
form.content: Subject + adverb of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) + main verb. EXCEPT with verb 'be': Subject + be + adverb.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Adverbs of Frequency
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Adverbs of Frequency.

controlledPractice.question: 'I ___ go to the cinema.' (70% of the time)
controlledPractice.explanation: Frequency adverbs usually go before the main verb: often go.

controlledPractice.question: 'She ___ late.' (100% of the time)
controlledPractice.explanation: With 'to be', the frequency adverb goes after the verb: is always.

controlledPractice.question: Which is the least frequent?
controlledPractice.explanation: Rarely sits near the 'never' end of the scale, around 10%.
